summary:
[  edit  ]
The Text  TOP  displays text strings in an image. It allows for multiple fonts, sizes, colors, borders, character separation and line separation. The text can be displayed as bit maps, anti-aliased lines, or filled polygon characters. Any TrueType font can be rendered by the Text  TOP .  Unicode  is supported.	The new Scalable Display Method uses  Slug Library  to render scalable, resolution independent text at the highest qulaity available in the Text  TOP .
It can display simple text strings with embedded numeric values. It can also format lines of text and numbers in decimal or floating point format, reading the numbers from a  CHOP , using special formatting characters.
It can also render text strings from a  Table DAT  via the Specification  DAT  parameter, where column headings are the parameter names that are to ve overidden when rendering a line of text for reach row of the table.
Any  TrueType  or  OpenType  font that has been loaded into Windows can be rendered by the Text  TOP . To import a new font into your Windows system, open the  Fonts  folder in the   Control Panel  , then drag and drop your   font files  in ( .ttf/.otf  file format). Fonts can also be specified as  .ttf/.otf  file paths in the Font File parameter.
You can render   Unicode   text by reading the text as a python string. See  Unicode .
Tip:  You can use the  textTOP_Class .textWidth member to calculate the width of the text in the Text  TOP .
See also:  Field COMP ,  Text SOP ,  Unicode .

inputs.description: Composite Input  - Control the Composite operation via the parameters on the Output Page of this operator.

parameters.label: Field  Component
parameters.name: field
parameters.description: Specifies a  Field Component  to use as the source of the text. The font and style of the text displayed in the Field  Component  are set using the parameters in the Text  TOP .

parameters.label: DAT
parameters.name: dat
parameters.description: Specifies a  DAT  to use for the source of the text. Drag and Drop a  DAT  onto this field, or manually enter the  DAT 's path.

parameters.label: DAT  Row
parameters.name: rowindex
parameters.description: The row number (starting from 0) of the cell, if the  DAT  is a table.

parameters.label: DAT  Col
parameters.name: colindex
parameters.description: The column number of the cell, if the  DAT  is a table.

parameters.label: Specification  DAT
parameters.name: specdat
parameters.description: A  Table DAT  that allows you to specify and position text by pixel, with the lower left corner being at 0, 0.  Column headers must include  position1  or  x ,  position2  or  y , and  text .  A sample table can be:

parameters.label: Text
parameters.name: text
parameters.description: A string of text. It optionally can be followed by a numeric value and another post-string, as set with  Value  and  Post Text  below. If newlines or tabs are desired, the recommended way is to change this parameter to expression mode, and specify a Python string that includes \n or \t to signify newlines and tabs. E.g 'First Line\nSecond Line'.

parameters.label: Legacy Parsing
parameters.name: legacyparsing
parameters.description: In older builds the syntax \XXX (E.g \200 would be character 200), \t, \n as well as [] and {} (to position strings) was parsed in the string. This is now deprecated. For specifying characters codes, \t and \n  Python syntax should be used instead. . The 'Specification  DAT ' should be used to position strings instead of [], {}. This parameter can be enabled to turn back on this legacy parsing though. If this is enabled and you want to display the characters  \ [ ] { } , you must precede them with a  \ .

parameters.label: Append Value
parameters.name: appendvalue
parameters.description: Enables the  Value  field defined below. This value is inserted between the  Text  string and the  Post Text  string.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.name: valuetouse
parameters.description: The numeric value to display.

parameters.label: Total Digits
parameters.name: totaldigits
parameters.description: The total number of digits in the value displayed.

parameters.label: Decimal Digits
parameters.name: decimaldigits
parameters.description: The number of digits displayed after the decimal place.

parameters.label: Post Text
parameters.name: posttext
parameters.description: The text string appended after Text and Value (if present).

parameters.label: CHOP  Value %-Replace
parameters.name: chopvaluereplace
parameters.description: Allows portions of the strings to be replaced by  CHOP  values via a syntax similar to C-style printf()/sprintf(). More details of the syntax are provided in the next parameter, ' CHOP ' .

parameters.label: CHOP
parameters.name: chop
parameters.description: The  CHOP  containing all the values to insert in the  Text  strings. The Text  TOP  will repeat the Text string until all  CHOP  channels are displayed. They are displayed by using a special syntax in your  Text  string, defined as string starting with  % , for example  %4d :

parameters.label: flags  (optional)
parameters.description: Alignment options.

parameters.label: width  (optional)
parameters.description: Total number of digits in the number displayed.

parameters.label: precision  (optional)
parameters.description: Number of digits after the decimal place.

parameters.label: type
parameters.description: Number format.

parameters.label: Word Wrap
parameters.name: wordwrap
parameters.description: When checked text is automatically line wrapped so it doesn't extend outside the  TOP 's borders.  When using Word Wrap and Auto-Size together, the text will first word-wrap based on the specified font size, then auto size the resulting block of text.

parameters.label: Smart Quote
parameters.name: smartquote
parameters.description: Enables smart quotes which use a left (opening) quotation mark and a right (closing) quotation mark instead of straight quotes.

parameters.label: Font
parameters.name: font
parameters.description: Select the font for the text from this drop down menu. All fonts are provided by Windows, any  TrueType  font that is loaded into Windows can be used.

parameters.label: Font File
parameters.name: fontfile
parameters.description: Specify any TrueType font file ( .ttf file ) to use for the text.  When using a font file, the Font menu above is disabled.

parameters.label: Character Set
parameters.name: charset
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select which character set to use.

parameters.label: Display Method
parameters.name: dispmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - The display method used.

parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.name: automatic
parameters.description: Automatically chooses which display mode to use based on font size and settings.

parameters.label: Polygon
parameters.name: polygon
parameters.description: Uses polygons to display the text. Polygons look better using large font sizes. They also support anti-aliasing (see Anti-Aliased below).

parameters.label: Stroke
parameters.name: stroke
parameters.description: Same as polygons but only an outline of the text is displayed.

parameters.label: Bitmap
parameters.name: bitmap
parameters.description: Uses bitmap images for the text. Bitmap fonts are better for very small font sizes where high precision is required.

parameters.label: Scalable
parameters.name: scalable
parameters.description: Uses  Slug Library  to render high-quality, scalable, resolution independent text.

parameters.label: Anti-Alias
parameters.name: antialias
parameters.description: ⊞  - Smoothes out the edges of the text. Not available for Texture Display Mode.

parameters.label: Stroke Width
parameters.name: strokewidth
parameters.description: Controls the width of the outline when using Stroke Display Method.

parameters.label: Bold
parameters.name: bold
parameters.description: Displays the text in  bold .

parameters.label: Italic
parameters.name: italic
parameters.description: Displays the text in  Italic .

parameters.label: Auto-Size Font
parameters.name: fontautosize
parameters.description: ⊞  - Automatically controls font size using one of the following 3 options. When using this feature along with Word Wrap turned on, it will first word-wrap the text based on the specified font size, then auto size the resulting block of text.

parameters.label: No Auto-Fit
parameters.name: nofit
parameters.description: Does not use any auto-fitting. Font Size specified in Font Size X and Font Size Y parameters.

parameters.label: Auto-Fit Always
parameters.name: alwaysfit
parameters.description: The font size will be increased or decreased so the text fits across the Text  TOP  from edge to edge.

parameters.label: Auto-Fit if Too Large
parameters.name: fitiffat
parameters.description: Only auto sizes the text if the text is too large and spills past the edges of the Text  TOP . In this case the font size will be decreased to fit it within the borders of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Font Size X
parameters.name: fontsizex
parameters.description: Sets the font size in X (horizontal).  Note:  Floating point font sizes are permissable when using   Polygon   and  Outline   Display Methods .

parameters.label: Font Size X Unit
parameters.name: fontsizexunit
parameters.description: Select the units for this parameter from Pixels, Fraction, Fraction Aspect or Points (font point size).	A Point is defined using the Windows conventions for 100% scaling, which is 96 pixels to 72 points. That is, a point size of 10 is the same as a pixel size of 10*(96/72) = 13.333.

parameters.label: Font Size Y
parameters.name: fontsizey
parameters.description: Sets the font size in Y (vertical).  Note:  Floating point font sizes are permissable when using   Polygon   and  Outline   Display Methods .

parameters.label: Font Size Y Unit
parameters.name: fontsizeyunit
parameters.description: Select the units for this parameter from Pixels, Fraction, Fraction Aspect or Points (font point size).

parameters.label: Keep Font Ratio
parameters.name: keepfontratio
parameters.description: Ignores Y value in Font Size. Sets both X and Y size to  Font Size  X.

parameters.label: Break Language
parameters.name: breaklang
parameters.description: Language type hint to help format the glyphs correctly.

parameters.label: Reading Direction
parameters.name: readingdirection
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use to set whether the language reads Left to Right or Right to Left.

parameters.label: Tracking
parameters.name: tracking
parameters.description: ⊞  - The amount of space to add between letters in X and Y. Tracking is way of adding an arbitrary offset between letters. There already is a default offset associated with each font so the letters are flush against each other. The Tracking parameter this adds to that and allows for a Y offset.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.name: position
parameters.description: ⊞  - The starting position of the text in X and Y.

parameters.label: [x,y]
parameters.description: "bleh[x,y]newtext"  will place  newtext  at position (x,y) on the screen.

parameters.label: {X,Y}
parameters.description: "bleh{(+/-)x,(+/-)y}newtext"  will offset  newtext  x,y from current position.

parameters.label: Position Unit
parameters.name: positionunit
parameters.description: Select the units for this parameter from Pixels, Fraction (0-1), Fraction Aspect (0-1 considering aspect ratio).

parameters.label: Line Spacing
parameters.name: linespacing
parameters.description: Determines the amount of space between lines of text.

parameters.label: Line Spacing Unit
parameters.name: linespacingunit
parameters.description: Select the units for this parameter from Pixels, Fraction (0-1), Fraction Aspect (0-1 considering aspect ratio).

parameters.label: Horizontal Align
parameters.name: alignx
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the horizontal alignment.

parameters.label: Left
parameters.name: left
parameters.description: Left justifies the text.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.name: center
parameters.description: Centers the text.

parameters.label: Right
parameters.name: right
parameters.description: Right justifies the text.

parameters.label: Horizontal Align Mode
parameters.name: alignxmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how horizontal alignment is calculated.

parameters.label: Use Font Metrics
parameters.name: metrics
parameters.description: Uses the font's built-in information to position the text.

parameters.label: Use Text Bounding Box
parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: Uses a bounding box around the text to position the text.

parameters.label: Vertical Align
parameters.name: aligny
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the vertical alignment.

parameters.label: Bottom
parameters.name: bottom
parameters.description: Bottom justifies the text.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.name: center
parameters.description: Centers the text.

parameters.label: Top
parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Top justifies the text.

parameters.label: Vertical Align Mode
parameters.name: alignymode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how vertical alignment is calculated.

parameters.label: Use Font Metrics
parameters.name: metrics
parameters.description: Uses the font's built-in information to position the text.

parameters.label: Use Text Bounding Box
parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: Uses a bounding box around the text to position the text.

parameters.label: Border Space
parameters.name: borderspace
parameters.description: ⊞  - When using Auto-Size Font, it will further shrink the text to give it a border.

parameters.label: Multiply RGB by Alpha
parameters.name: multrgbbyalpha
parameters.description: Multiplies the RGB channels by the alpha channel.

parameters.label: Font Color
parameters.name: fontcolor
parameters.description: ⊞  - RGBA values for the text displayed. (default: white (1,1,1,1))

parameters.label: Font Alpha
parameters.name: fontalpha
parameters.description: Set the alpha value for the font.

parameters.label: Background Color
parameters.name: bgcolor
parameters.description: ⊞  - RGBA values for the background. (default: black (0,0,0,0))

parameters.label: Background Alpha
parameters.name: bgalpha
parameters.description: Set the alpha value for the background.

parameters.label: Border A
parameters.name: bordera
parameters.description: ⊞  - RGBA values for border A color.

parameters.label: Border A Alpha
parameters.name: borderaalpha
parameters.description: Set the alpha value for border A.

parameters.label: Border B
parameters.name: borderb
parameters.description: ⊞  - RGBA values for border B color.

parameters.label: Border B Alpha
parameters.name: borderbalpha
parameters.description: Set the alpha value for border B.

parameters.label: Left Border
parameters.name: leftborder
parameters.description: What color the 2 left-most pixels are. Options are 0 (no change), Border A (uses color defined in Border A), or Border B (uses color defined in Border B).

parameters.label: Left Border Inside
parameters.name: leftborderi
parameters.description: Same as above parameter but used for an inside border.

parameters.label: Right Border
parameters.name: rightborder
parameters.description: What color the 2 right-most pixels are. Options are 0 (no change), Border A (uses color defined in Border A), or Border B (uses color defined in Border B).

parameters.label: Right Border Inside
parameters.name: rightborderi
parameters.description: Same as above parameter but used for an inside border.

parameters.label: Bottom Border
parameters.name: bottomborder
parameters.description: What color the 2 bottom-most pixels are. Options are 0 (no change), Border A (uses color defined in Border A), or Border B (uses color defined in Border B).

parameters.label: Bottom Border Inside
parameters.name: bottomborderi
parameters.description: Same as above parameter but used for an inside border.

parameters.label: Top Border
parameters.name: topborder
parameters.description: What color the 2 top-most pixels are. Options are 0 (no change), Border A (uses color defined in Border A), or Border B (uses color defined in Border B).

parameters.label: Top Border Inside
parameters.name: topborderi
parameters.description: Same as above parameter but used for an inside border.

parameters.label: Comp Over Input
parameters.name: compoverinput
parameters.description: Turning this On will composite the input with the image.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.name: operand
parameters.description: ⊞  - Choose which composite operation is performed from this menu. Search the web for 'blend modes' for more detailed information on the effects of each type.

parameters.label: Add
parameters.name: add
parameters.description: input1.rgba + input2.rgba

parameters.label: Atop
parameters.name: atop
parameters.description: (input1.rgba * input2.a) + (input2.rgba * (1.0 - input1.a))

parameters.label: Average
parameters.name: average
parameters.description: (input1.rgba + input2.rgba)/2

parameters.label: Difference
parameters.name: difference
parameters.description: absoluteValue(input1.rgb - input2.rgb). Alpha always equals 1.0

parameters.label: Divide
parameters.name: divide
parameters.description: input1.rgba  / input2.rgba

parameters.label: Inside
parameters.name: inside
parameters.description: input1.rgba * clamp(input2.a, 0.0, 1.0)

parameters.label: Maximum
parameters.name: maximum
parameters.description: max(input1.r, input2.r), max(input1.g, input2.g), max(input1.b, input2.b), max(input1.a, input2.a)

parameters.label: Minimum
parameters.name: minimum
parameters.description: min(input1.r, input2.r), min(input1.g, input2.g), min(input1.b, input2.b), min(input1.a, input2.a)

parameters.label: Outside
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: input1.rgba * (1.0 - input2.a)

parameters.label: Over
parameters.name: over
parameters.description: (input2.rgba * (1.0 - input1.a)) + input1.rgba

parameters.label: Screen
parameters.name: screen
parameters.description: 1.0 - ((1.0 - input1.rgba) * (1.0 - input2.rgba))

parameters.label: Subtract
parameters.name: subtract
parameters.description: input1.rgba - input2.rgba

parameters.label: Under
parameters.name: under
parameters.description: (input1.rgba * (1.0 - input2.a)) + input2.rgba

parameters.label: Xor
parameters.name: xor
parameters.description: (input1.rgba * (1.0 - input2.a)) + (input2.rgba * (1.0 - input1.a))

parameters.label: Swap Order
parameters.name: swaporder
parameters.description: Swaps the order of the composite with the input.

parameters.label: Output  Resolution
parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - quickly change the resolution of the  TOP 's data.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution

parameters.label: Eighth
parameters.name: eighth
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Quarter
parameters.name: quarter
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Half
parameters.name: half
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 2X
parameters.name: 2x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 4X
parameters.name: 4x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 8X
parameters.name: 8x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Grow or shrink the input resolution to fit this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit the input resolution to be not larger than this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Directly control the width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine how the  TOP  image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.name: best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail. When the input is 32-bit float format, only nearest filtering will be used (regardless of what is selected).

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the  GLSL TOP  when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected  TOP 's image.

parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the  TOP  will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to  Pixel Formats  for more information.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace. Note that this does  not  apply an sRGB curve to the pixel values, it only stores them using an sRGB curve. This means more data is used for the darker values and less for the brighter values. When the values are read downstream they will be converted back to linear. For more information refer to  sRGB .

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)

parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue  Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono8fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono16fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono)

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RG)

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RG)

Las primitivas de punto, por ejemplo, son primitivas de un solo vértice renderizadas como puntos, ideales para nubes de puntos o sistemas de partículas.7 Una distinción clave con respecto a los SOPs es que los POPs actualmente no admiten primitivas de curva directamente, aunque la subdivisión de splines es posible utilizando operadores como Line POP y Line Divide POP.7 Los atributos son cruciales para almacenar datos adicionales por punto, vértice o primitiva, como normales (N), coordenadas de textura (uv) y color (Cd).1 Los POPs permiten la creación, modificación, duplicación, cambio de nombre y eliminación de estos atributos.1 El énfasis en los "atributos" y su manipulación a través de varios POPs (por ejemplo, Attribute POP, GLSL POP, Math Mix POP) apunta a una filosofía de diseño centrada en los atributos para los POPs. Muchos POPs (Attribute POP, GLSL POP, Math Mix POP, etc.) están explícitamente diseñados para crear, modificar o combinar atributos.1 La documentación destaca que los

ivide POP: Se utiliza para subdividir cualquier tira de línea. • Experimental:Line Metrics POP: Genera nuevos atributos, a menudo de tipo entero sin signo, con nombres predeterminados. Por ejemplo, puede generar el atributo Dir (dirección). • Experimental:Line POP: Un operador que permite la creación de tiras de línea. Puede dividir curvas o generar puntos de control con atributos que definen la forma de la curva, como Weight o Tension. También permite crear y modificar atributos de color y textura. • Experimental:Line Smooth POP: Puede añadir puntos y suavizar líneas. • Experimental:Line Thick POP: El material de línea (Line MAT) de TouchDesigner se implementa internamente usando una conversión a este POP, lo que sugiere su rol en la representación visual de líneas. • Experimental:Lookup Attribute POP: Utiliza uno, dos o tres componentes de un atributo como índices para realizar búsquedas. También puede utilizar atributos de solo lectura. • Experimental:Lookup Channel POP: Sim

Por ejemplo, para crear un mapa de calor donde los valores más bajos son 0 y los más altos son 1. * **Null POP (POP Nulo)** * **Función principal:** Este es un operador muy simple que **no hace nada**; simplemente pasa la información de su entrada a su salida sin cambios. * **Características clave:** * **No consume CPU o memoria GPU** para los atributos que no modifica, ya que sol

ás creando ya existe. --- #### 5. Attribute POP * **¿Qué hace?** Este operador es fundamental para la gestión de atributos. Te permite **crear nuevos atributos**, **renombrar atributos existentes**, **duplicarlos** o **eliminarlos**. * **Características clave:** * **Crear nuevos atributos**: Cuando creas uno, puedes especificar: * Su **nombre** (puedes usar nombres predefinidos como `P` para posición, `N` para normales, `Color` para color, `Tex` para coordenadas de textura, o crear el tuyo propio). * Su **tipo de dato** (`float`, `double`, `int`, `uint`). * El **número de componentes** (1, 2, 3 o 4). Por ejemplo, un `float` con 3 componentes es un `float3`. * Si es un **array** (lista de valores) y su tamaño. * Un **valor por defecto** para cada componente. * También puede crear **atributos de matriz** (como `mat4x4`). * **Renombrar atributos**: Simplemente cambias el nombre de un atributo existente
